newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill elderly man in troubled Pakistani city.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill elderly man in troubled Pakistani city.

text.p: Masked gunmen killed a 60-year-old man at his home in the Malir district of the southern port city of Karachi on Thursday, police said. The murder of Abdul Nabi, whose political affiliation was not immediately known, was the latest incident in a surge of ethnic and sectarian violence in the city, where at least 12 people have been killed in the past three days. Para military troops were patrolling District East on Thursday after supporters of the Haqiqi splinter faction of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) burned two vehicles, forced shops to close and blocked traffic, witnesses said.
The MQM-Haqiqi activists were protesting at Tuesday's attack on their headquarters in which gunmen killed two party workers.

MQM-Haqiqi leader Afaq Ahmed blamed the government, rather than the mainstream MQM, for the assault. Karachi police chief Malik Mohammad Iqbal rejected the accusation. The MQM, now part of the Sindh province coalition government, has long feuded with the MQM-Haqiqi faction. More than 50 people have been killed in ethnic, political and sectarian violence in Karachi this year, compared to 500 last year and about 2,000 in 1995.
